rubric: The chart is an honest, readable form for a 12-week trend: a baseline that starts at zero or is clearly marked, labelled units, and no distorted scale.
The chart is labelled directly or with a minimal axis: few gridlines, no heavy borders, no legend for a single series, and the title says what is shown.
Table numbers are right-aligned with consistent decimals and currency formatting, and the columns are easy to scan.
Colour is restrained: one main colour for the data, with any highlight used on purpose rather than for decoration.
Chart and table form one coherent page with clear hierarchy, and nothing is clipped or overflowing.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both pages fit on one screen, use zero-baseline bar charts and right-align their numbers. A uses one muted colour with a single highlighted bar and an insight title, though the dashed average line runs through several bar labels. B adds a legend and four bright highlighted bars over dark brown ones, which is heavier, and its PRODUCT header is right-aligned over left-aligned names. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use honest zero-baseline bar charts with dollar axes and clean, right-aligned tables. In B, the dashed 12-week average line runs through several bar labels (6.7k, 6.9k, 6.7k), which makes the chart look cluttered. B also has more gridlines than it needs, though its single highlighted bar is more restrained. A is cleaner overall and its orange highlight marks the reporting period on purpose, but its chart panel leaves empty space and its PRODUCT header is oddly right-aligned.
